newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Coal/Allied says profits under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Coal/Allied says profits under pressure.

text.p: Coal producer Coal and Allied Industries Ltd said on Friday that price reductions for semi-soft coking coal and thermal coal would place pressure on profitability in the immediate future.
Chairman David Klingner said the past year had seen demand for each type of coal remain strong.
"However a growing oversupply of thermal coal has occurred as production in Auistralia has increased due to new mines starting up and existing mines increasing capacity."
The company is 71-percent owned by Australian-Anglo mining house CRA Ltd-RTZ Plc.
Klingner said negotiations for coal deliveries to Japan from April 1, the start of that country's fiscal year, had led to price falls for both coking and thermal coal.
The effect of these reductions, flowing on from last year's negotiations, would "place pressure on profitability in the immediate future".
Klingner said the price falls would also flow to customers in other countries.
"As a consequence 1997 is looming as a watershed year for the Australian coal industry and your company," he told shareholders at the annual general meerting.
Australian coal producers accepted a cut of US$2.00 per tonne for semi-soft coals to Japan and a US$2.65 per tonne cut for thermal coal deliveries from April 1.
Klingner said the company had to ensure that it improved its efficiencies to compete in a tight market.
Coal and Allied, whose mining operations are based in the state of New South Wales, suffered a slump in calendar 1996 net profit to A$4.06 million from A$41.99 million in 1995.
